events.title: Grand jury indicts John Caravello on felony assault charges
events.summary: In September 2026, a federal grand jury indicted John Caravello on felony assault charges stemming from his actions during the Glass House Farms protest on 10 July 2026. The indictment carried a potential sentence of up to 20 years in prison. Caravello was released on bond pending trial, which took place in April 2026 and resulted in acquittal.
events.why_relevant: The indictment of a protester for resisting chemical weapons deployment represents prosecutorial use of the criminal justice system to suppress dissent and chill political participation in immigration enforcement protests.
events.basis: In September, a grand jury indicted him for felony assault. He faced up to 20 years behind bars.

events.title: National Industrial Security Program Policy Advisory Committee (NISPPAC) meeting announced for September 2, 2026.
events.summary: The Information Security Oversight Office (ISOO) at the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) announced a public meeting of the National Industrial Security Program Policy Advisory Committee (NISPPAC) scheduled for September 2, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. ET. The hybrid meeting will be held in the McGowan Theater at 701 Constitution Ave. NW, Washington, DC, with virtual attendance available via Zoom for Gov. The Committee will discuss National Industrial Security Program policy matters. Public registration is required in advance.
events.why_relevant: Federal advisory committee meetings open to the public are a mechanism for transparency and public participation in government policy deliberation on classified-information security matters.
events.basis: We are announcing an upcoming National Industrial Security Program Policy Advisory Committee (NISPPAC) meeting in accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act and implementing regulations.
